newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices flat, Anaheim ahead.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS - prices flat, Anaheim ahead.

text.p: U.S. municipal bond prices were unchanged in quiet early trade as players readied for mid-morning economic data and a $459 million Anaheim Public Finance Authority deal.
"There's not much going on today," a trader said. "We get leading indicators and home sales at 10 o'clock (1000 EST), so those have the potential to move the market a little bit."

The Commerce Department is expected to issue data on December single-family home sales at 1000 EST. Economists surveyed by Reuters expect, on average, that new home sales will slip to an annualized 745,000 in December from an annualized 772,000 in November.
Also at 1000 EST, the Conference Board is expected to issue its index of leading economic indicators. Economists expect the December index to be up 0.1 percent after a 0.1 percent November gain.
Earlier Tuesday, U.S. chain store sales came in unchanged for the week ended February 1 from the prior week, according to the seasonally adjusted BTM/Schroders weekly chain store sales index.

Tuesday also marks the first leg of the Federal Reserve's Federal Open Market Committee's two-day meeting. No word regarding short-term rates is expected until Wednesday, though policy makers are expected to leave short-term rates unchanged.

Actively quoted municipal issues Tuesday included Denver, Colo., City & County Airport 5-1/2 percent revenue refunding bonds of November 2025. The bonds had a 5.79 percent net bid, unchanged from Monday's close.
However, Delaware River Port Authority, Pa. & N.J., 5-1/2 percent bonds of January 2026 showed weakness. Bonds had a 5.70 percent net bid versus a 5.66 percent net bid on Monday.
Overall secondary activity was light, a second trader agreed.
"There hasn't been much trading," a trader said. "There's only one bid wanted list out there right now, it's a decent size though."
The customer list contained eight items each averaging about $2.5 million, the trader said.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was down 5/32 at 96-25/32 to yield 6.75 percent. In debt futures, the December municipal contract was down 4/32 at 115-23/32. The March T-bond contract was down 3/32 at 112. The MOB spread was 119 ticks.
Turning to new issues, "the big deal this week is this Anaheim deal," a trader said. The deal is one of nine negotiated sales set for Tuesday totaling $737 million.
Proceeds from the revenue bond sale, expected via senior manager PaineWebber Inc., will pay for public improvements that will help Walt Disney Co's theme park, Disneyland.
Fourteen competitive sales are slated, totaling $119 million. The largest is a $25 million Forsyth County School District, Ga., at 1100 EST.
